title: Chipmunk interop regression harness for partial-JSON recovery and toolcall fallback behavior
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build a deterministic regression harness (codename: Chipmunk) that validates end-to-end API compatibility across streaming, tool/function calls, and structured outputs with a focus on partial-JSON responses and fallback semantics. The harness will run both locally and in CI, produce golden-seed test vectors, and provide clear signal for flaky regressions vs. intentional behavior changes. This ticket covers design, seed corpus curation, harness implementation, CI integration, and initial runbook for triage.
acceptance_criteria: Chipmunk harness can execute a suite of 250+ scenarios (streaming, interleaved toolcalls, structured outputs) producing deterministic fingerprints
Harness flags partial-JSON situations and validates configured fallback behavior (retry, schema-fallback, tool-retry) against golden expectations
CI job runs harness on merge to main and blocks release branches on high-severity contract regressions
Artifacts (seed prompts, golden outputs, failure diffs) are persisted to the conformance bucket and linked in CI logs
Documentation exists: README, triage runbook, and example GitHub PR annotations for failures
tasks: Design harness API and test vector schema (seed/prompt/meta/expected) - Aisha
Implement streaming simulator for partial chunk injection and re-ordering - Marcus
Create golden-seed corpus (initial 250 scenarios) with coverage matrix - Eng QA
Add assertion layer for function/toolcall idempotency and fallback paths - Marcus
Integrate harness into CI as conformance job with artifact upload - DevOps
Write triage runbook and PR annotation tooling for failed runs - Aisha
test_plan: Unit tests for simulator (deterministic replay of chunk sequences)
Property tests to fuzz partial-JSON boundary cases and ensure graceful parser recovery
Cross-model smoke runs (redwood-1, open-quant) to detect model-specific stream quirks
Canary CI job that runs fast subset on every PR and nightly full run against main
Regression verification comparing current run fingerprints to golden seeds and producing unified diff summaries
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff complete; design doc posted to Confluence (https://confluence.redwood/c/chipmunk-design). Decided to store golden seeds in gs://redwood-conformance/chipmunk/seed-v1.
2026-03-03 - Marcus Nguyen: Prototype simulator implemented; supports injecting truncated JSON tokens and simulating interleaved toolcall messages. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4892

2026-03-05 - Eng QA (Riley Torres): Seed curation started. Goal to prioritize user-facing toolcall patterns (function-call with streaming partial responses, NDJSON edges, and nested structured outputs).

2026-03-07 - Marcus Nguyen: Noted trade-off: strict schema enforcement will catch intentional behavioral changes from model upgrades; we'll add per-scenario sensitivity flags (strict|lenient) to reduce noisy failures.
2026-03-09 - Aisha Patel: CI integration draft pipeline created (conformance/chipmunk.yml). Running nightly full-suite and PR-fast-suite. DevOps to add artifact retention policy.
2026-03-10 - Marcus Nguyen: Observed flakiness on model redwood-quant-2 in 12/250 seeds (time-based chunk reorder); opened follow-up ENG-86557 to investigate kernel scheduling interactions.
notes: Design trade-offs: prefer deterministic replay over probabilistic sampling to make CI actionable.
We will expose an optional --update-golden flag for approved behavior changes and require a 2-person review to update seeds.
Plan to publish a short dashboard in Console for conformance pass rate by model, region, and commit.
